prerequisites: It is recommended that students have taken courses related to Programming (especially the Algorithmics course).
Knowledge of computer hardware (Computer Fundamentals and Networks and Computer Architecture courses) and operating systems (Operating Systems course).
Ability to read and understand texts written in English for part of the bibliography.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and implement the parallel programming paradigm based on distributed memory and message passing, shared memory, and heterogeneous/hybrid models.
Select the appropriate parallel programming paradigm for a given problem.
Evaluate the gain of a parallel solution compared to the equivalent single-processor version.
Develop a parallel solution that meets a given specification.
Understand the concept of execution thread and know its programming models.
Select the appropriate threading programming model for a given problem specification.
Know the synchronization mechanisms between threads. Understand and prevent their problems. Apply appropriate synchronization mechanisms to a given problem.
Develop an efficient and effective multi-threaded solution for a given problem specification.
Evaluate the gain of a multi-threaded solution compared to the equivalent single-threaded version.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Presentation and State of the Art.
Performance Models and Analysis of Parallel Algorithms: Execution time, efficiency, speed-up, cost, scalability, etc.
Design of Parallel Algorithms: Decomposition, assignment, balancing, overlapping, partitioning, etc. Relaxed algorithms, pipeline, master-slave, process farm and replicated, etc.
Concurrent and Parallel Environments: Concurrency: basic concepts, models and synchronization mechanisms. Parallelism: programming models. Accelerators and hybrid-heterogeneous solutions.

assessment_methods.method: Partial exam (P1) on Performance and Design topics
Partial exam (P2) on Concurrent and Parallel Environments topics

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade (Nota) is calculated as 0.5 * Theory + 0.5 * Practicals. Theory is a weighted sum of partial exams, and Practicals is the arithmetic mean of graded practical sessions. A final score of 5 or more (out of 10) is required to pass. Uncompleted activities are graded with a zero; if their total weight exceeds 50% of the final grade, the student will receive "No presentado". In the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a theoretical exam (50%) and a practical exam (50%), requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 to pass. In case of doubt about authorship or unauthorized means (e.g., AI tools), students may be asked for an in-person defense.
